newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish yields follow Europe lower.
newsitem.headline: Swedish yields follow Europe lower.

text.p: Yields fell in calm late trade in line with stronger European markets. The crown was unchanged against the German mark. The market is waiting for U.S. statistics due next week. * Six month T-bill rate fell two basis points to 4.15 pct. * Ten year bond yield fell two basis points to 7.24 pct. * The crown was unchanged at 4.4620 crowns to the mark versus 4.4615 crowns on Wednesday. (Details/background follows)
STOCKHOLM, April 24 (Reuter) - Swedish bond yields ended lower in line with stronger European markets on Thursday and the crown was unchanged against the mark.

"Yields fell because the market opened on a positive note this morning when the crown was stronger and European yields lower," a trader said. "Since then there has barely been any activity in Europe."

The crown strengthened initially on a generally weaker mark but softened in late trading to end flat at 4.4620 to mark compared to 4.4615 late on Wednesday. The six-month T-bill rate fell two basis points to 4.15 percent.
The ten-year bond yield dropped two basis points to 7.24 percent.
German statistics showing a falling consumer price index (CPI) supported European bond yields, dealers said.
The Swedish Riksbank left, as expected, its key rates unchanged at its Thursday board meeting.
Next week the market will focus on a slew of U.S. statistics, including unemployment and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figures.
